subject.title: Node host: no SSH transport support + challenge auth fails behind reverse proxy

question: Should node-host get first-class managed SSH transport, and what trust boundary should apply to reverse-proxy remote node pairing?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but implementing it changes SSH process lifecycle and whether loopback/tunneled or proxied endpoints can affect node-role approval and remote command execution authority.

options.title: Design managed node-host SSH
options.body: Keep this issue open for a scoped design that adds node-host SSH only with explicit host-key policy, service lifecycle behavior, pairing locality rules, docs, and live reverse-proxy proof.

options.title: Keep SSH external
options.body: Maintain the current manual SSH tunnel contract and focus on docs, diagnostics, and device-pairing recovery for reverse-proxy node hosts.

options.title: Split auth to the remote-node issue
options.body: Let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91126 own node approval/auth policy while this issue tracks only the SSH transport decision.

recommendation.title: Design managed node-host SSH
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a scoped design that adds node-host SSH only with explicit host-key policy, service lifecycle behavior, pairing locality rules, docs, and live reverse-proxy proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history ties this decision to the node daemon, gateway auth, and SSH transport surfaces he introduced or refactored.
